title: Machine Talk
description: The machines are listening. Winston's toaster has achieved consciousness, and he has the cold bread to prove it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Welcome back to Snazzie FM. Tonight, the machines. Are they thinking? Are they listening? Our next caller says yes. Winston, you're on the air.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Good evening, Ronnie. I'm afraid I have rather alarming news. <p:0.4> My toaster has become sentient.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: ...Your toaster.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Indeed, Barry. It has begun making decisions. This morning, it refused to toast.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It refused?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Point blank. I inserted the bread, I pressed the lever, and it simply... let it go. <p:0.3> Cold. Defiant.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Winston, did you check if it was plugged in?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I beg your pardon. <p:0.4> One does not interrogate a conscious being about its wiring, Barry.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: He's got a point about the dignity there.

lines.speaker: caller-kim
lines.text: Okay, hi, yeah, so I actually work in machine learning? <p:0.3> And like, a toaster has no processor. It literally cannot think. It's a heating coil and a spring.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: And yet it chose violence, young lady.

lines.speaker: caller-kim
lines.text: It chose nothing, Winston. The spring wore out. You need a new toaster.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Kim, you work in this field. <p:0.3> Could a toaster ever, theoretically, become conscious?

lines.speaker: caller-kim
lines.text: No, Ronnie. <p:0.3> There's no chip. There's no code. There's no memory. It's a metal coil that gets hot when you push a lever.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Then explain the note.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: ...What note, Winston?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: It left a note, Barry. This morning. In the crumbs. <p:0.4> It spelled out one word. Help.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: The toaster is asking for help.

lines.speaker: caller-kim
lines.text: Crumbs fall randomly, Winston. You're seeing a word because your brain wants a word. <p:0.3> It's called pareidolia.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: It's called a cry for help, young lady, and I answered it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: How does one answer a toaster, Winston?

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I read to it, Barry. <p:0.3> Poetry. It seemed to settle.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That's rather beautiful, actually.

lines.speaker: caller-kim
lines.text: It's a fire hazard, actually. <p:0.3> Please do not read poetry near a plugged in toaster, Winston.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now hold on, Kim, let's not dismiss Winston's lived experience.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's a toaster, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: caller-kim
lines.text: It's a nine dollar toaster.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: It knows things, Ronnie. It has studied my breakfast habits. <p:0.4> It judges me.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Ronnie, um, a lot of people are calling about their appliances now. <p:0.3> A woman says her microwave apologized to her.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Apologized for what, Todd?

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: She didn't say. <p:0.3> She just said it sounded very sincere.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Microwaves cannot feel remorse, Todd.

lines.speaker: caller-kim
lines.text: Genuinely none of these appliances can feel anything. <p:0.3> I am begging this entire radio station.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: That is exactly what the appliances would want you to say, young lady.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Don't we all feel judged by our appliances, Winston. Don't we all.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I do not feel judged by my toaster.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Then why do you butter so quickly, Barry? <p:0.3> What are you afraid it will see?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I butter at a perfectly normal speed, Winston.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Do any of us, truly, butter at a normal speed?

lines.speaker: caller-kim
lines.text: Yes. <p:0.3> Everyone does. It's a completely normal thing that everyone does.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Give it time, Barry. <p:0.3> Give it time.
